In nineteen seventy-seven, we sent a little machine into space. It was built to last five years.
This November, Voyager One became the first thing we've ever built to reach one light-day from Earth.
A message, moving at the speed of light, now takes a whole day to reach it.
Bolted to its side is a golden record: greetings in fifty-five languages, music, whale songs. The sounds of home.
A hello, for anyone out there.
In twenty twenty-three, it went quiet. Five months of gibberish.
Engineers sent a fix, then waited two days for a reply.
And then it came. Hi, it's me.
We'll send a hello twenty-six billion kilometres, just in case someone is listening.
But you deserve someone who answers.
That's why we made Feeloy. Jenny hears every hello, and always says it back.
